question: If 16% of people are Rh-negative and couples pair at random, what % of pregnancies pair an Rh-negative mother with an Rh-positive baby?
move: A parent showing a trait is not the same as passing it on.
ask: What trait am I assuming someone will pass on, just because they have it?
trap: Multiplying 16% by 84% Rh-positive fathers, as if each passes it on.
hint: Not every Rh-positive father passes the gene on; start from how common the gene is.
steps: Rh-negative means two copies of the d gene, so d's share is the square root of 0.16 = 0.4.
A random father passes on the Rh-positive gene with chance 1 - 0.4 = 0.6.
source: Hartl & Clark, Principles of Population Genetics
reference: Hartl & Clark, Principles of Population Genetics, 4th edition, Sinauer Associates, 2007
